subject: Re: Escalation: repeated 503/timeouts during traffic spikes (us-east) — Asteria Health
body:
From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@asteriahealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mark Liu <mark.liu@asteriahealth.com>
Date: Mon, Nov 10, 2025 at 8:12 AM PT
Subject: Escalation: repeated 503/timeouts during traffic spikes (us-east)

Rafael,

Escalating per Sean’s note from last quarter that we should reach out directly if we see reliability regressions.

Over the last 10 days we’ve had repeated timeouts / 503s on the Hosted API in us-east, almost always during our predictable AM traffic spikes (08:45–10:15 ET). This is impacting a production clinical workflow.

Symptoms:
- Requests stall and then time out at our client (60s), with a mix of 503 and 5xx.
- We also see disconnects on streaming responses.
- Retries sometimes succeed, but we’ve had bursts where retries pile up and the situation gets worse.

We need:
1) A clear explanation of what’s happening and whether this is a Redwood capacity issue.
2) Guidance on what to change client-side immediately.
3) Timeline on when this is going to stop.

We’re on the endpoint we were told to use for Hosted in us-east. Model is rw-chat-3 (pinned).

Can you advise today? Happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Priya
Director of Engineering
Asteria Health


---

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@asteriahealth.com>
Cc: Mark Liu <mark.liu@asteriahealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Nov 10, 2025 at 8:37 AM PT
Subject: Re: Escalation: repeated 503/timeouts during traffic spikes (us-east)

Priya — thank you for flagging, and sorry you’re dealing with this.

High level: what you’re describing matches an overload pattern we’ve been actively addressing. Under sharp spikes, the current Hosted request path can degrade into long queueing (and then timeouts / ambiguous 5xx) rather than failing fast with clear retry guidance.

We have a program in flight specifically to prevent this failure mode (“circuit breakers + load shedding”), but that doesn’t help you this morning unless we give you interim guardrails.

Two immediate asks so I can confirm the exact overload signature on our side:
1) Can you send 5–10 request IDs (or your correlation IDs) from the 08:45–10:15 ET window, including a couple that timed out and a couple that returned 503?
2) If possible, share a small sample of client logs showing retry behavior (even sanitized).

In the meantime, interim mitigation guidance (safe defaults):
- Cap concurrency for this route/model during spike windows (we can help pick a number once we see your traffic profile).
- If you retry on failures, use exponential backoff with jitter, and do NOT immediately retry timeouts in a tight loop. If you have a global retry middleware, make sure it’s not retrying streaming disconnects aggressively.
- If you can tolerate it, reduce max output tokens during peak windows (reduces decode contention).
- If you can accept a fallback, we can discuss a temporary policy to fail over to a compatible model variant or alternate region during brownouts (depends on your pinning requirements).

Timeline: we’re canarying the first breaker/shedding changes in us-east starting next week, then expanding. I’ll give you a concrete date once I confirm where rw-chat-3 sits in the rollout order.

If you’re available, I can do a 20 min call today between 11:00–14:00 PT.

Rafael Mendes
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks. Attaching sanitized logs + request samples.

We see timeouts first, then a wave of 503s. Our client currently retries up to 3 times with a fixed 250ms delay (no jitter). That’s probably on us, but we implemented it because we didn’t have consistent Retry-After guidance.

A few request IDs (Redwood response header x-redwood-request-id):
- rwd_01HFWZ2K9M2M0E2M6A7T6X2Q0V (timeout client-side)
- rwd_01HFWZ39J7E7H6V9QZ1B9W6B2P (503)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@asteriahealth.com>
Cc: Mark Liu <mark.liu@asteriahealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Amara Diallo <amara_diallo@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Nov 10, 2025 at 10:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: Escalation: repeated 503/timeouts during traffic spikes (us-east)

Priya — this is very helpful.

We pulled the request IDs you sent. The pattern is consistent with pool saturation + queue growth on the Hosted us-east GPU pool serving rw-chat-3 during that window. When queue depth crosses a threshold, we see tail latency collapse and downstream timeouts (client sees 60s). The 503s are coming later when parts of the path start rejecting, but today it’s not consistently “fail fast,” which is why you’re seeing a mix.

Important: your fixed-delay retries (250ms, 3x, no jitter) will amplify this under overload. It’s a totally reasonable default when errors are rare, but during saturation it creates a retry storm and makes the queue even worse.

Recommended client-side changes (you can implement today):
1) Switch retries to exponential backoff with jitter.
   - Example starting point: base=500ms, factor=2, max_delay=8s, jitter=full.
   - Max attempts: 2 (total 3 tries including the first). Under overload, more than that typically hurts both you and the platform.
2) Only retry when the error is explicitly retryable.
   - If you get 503, retryable.
   - If you get a timeout, treat it as retryable but with a longer backoff (and do not retry streaming disconnects more than once).
3) Add a cap on in-flight requests per host / worker.
   - If you tell me your typical concurrency and RPS during the spike window, we can suggest a safe cap to avoid queue blowups.
4) If you can, reduce max_tokens during the spike window and/or reduce parallel batch jobs that share the same model route.

What we’ll do server-side (timeline):
- We are rolling out circuit breakers + deterministic load shedding to Hosted. The goal is: during overload we fail early at the edge with a consistent 429/503 response and explicit Retry-After, instead of letting requests sit in a queue until they time out.
- Current plan for us-east:
  - Canary enablement starting week of Nov 17 for a subset of models/routes.
  - Expand through the week of Nov 24 if metrics look good.
  - rw-chat-3 is targeted in the first wave (subject to final validation).

Interim mitigation we can offer on our side:
- We can temporarily bias routing for your org away from the hottest shard within us-east during the spike window (limited lever, but it can help).
- If you can accept a region fallback, we can discuss a controlled failover option (us-west) for only the overload case. This is safer once the breaker rollout is live, because it avoids endless fallback loops.

Dev (cc’d) can also share a short retry snippet we recommend (language-specific) if that helps your team move quickly.

If you’re free, I can do a call at 11:30 PT with you + Mark.

Rafael

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mark Liu <mark.liu@asteriahealth.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@asteriahealth.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Nov 10, 2025 at 10:46 AM PT
Subject: Re: Escalation: repeated 503/timeouts during traffic spikes (us-east)

Mark — both good questions.

1) 429 vs 503
We’ll use both, but with consistent semantics:
- 429: admission control / overload protection at the edge (we’re telling you “too many requests right now,” usually the best signal for client backoff).
- 503: service temporarily unavailable due to capacity saturation / breaker open (e.g., per model/region/tier).

The important change vs today is that these will be intentional and consistent (not ambiguous gateway 5xx), and we’ll include explicit retry guidance via Retry-After where applicable.

For your client logic: treat both 429 and 503 as retryable with backoff + jitter. Avoid tight loops.

2) Billing for failed/timeouts
For Hosted:
- Requests rejected before generation (i.e., we shed early / breaker open) are not billed for output tokens (and generally not billed for input tokens either if we never accepted the request into the runtime).
- If a request runs and produces tokens and then disconnects mid-stream, you may see billed tokens corresponding to work actually performed. This is one reason we’re prioritizing “fail fast” during overload instead of letting requests sit and partially execute.

If you send us a couple of invoice line items / timestamps that look suspicious, Dev can help correlate with request IDs and confirm.

Also attaching a quick Grafana snapshot from our side for the timeframe you referenced (queue depth + shed events). This is for context; we’ll walk through on the call.

Attachment:
- grafana-snapshot-us-east-queue-depth-2025-11-10.png

See you at 11:30 PT.

Rafael

Subject: Re: Escalation: repeated 503/timeouts during traffic spikes (us-east)

Priya/Mark — following up from the call.

As discussed, here are the concrete client-side changes we recommend you ship this week:
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with full jitter; max 2 retries; do not retry streaming disconnects more than once.
- Respect Retry-After when present.
- Add an in-flight cap per worker (start with 8; adjust after we watch your metrics for 48h).

Rafael is tracking the server-side rollout and will update you once rw-chat-3 is enabled in the us-east canary.

If it’s useful, we can schedule a 30 min working session with your team to review retry middleware and make sure there isn’t an unintended retry loop.

Dev Patel
Customer Support & Reliability Liaison
Redwood Inference
